Senses.Note: Zen bends an ordinary degree phrase by making it a named category explicitly defined against small doubt and repeatedly paired with great awakening. The family comparison with doubt-mass (疑情) and ball of doubt (疑團) supports one sense, not a noun/verb split: both constructions name the same doubt.

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Great doubt is an intensified mass of inquiry cultivated until its obstruction breaks open.
EvidenceBody: The phrase occurs 196 times in 91 allowlisted texts. A direct definition says, ‘doubt has no large or small; only when the doubt is weighty is it called great doubt, and when light it is called small doubt’ (疑。情無大小，但疑之重，是謂大疑；疑之輕，是謂小疑). The same record says that when one cannot refrain from raising it, ‘therefore it is named great doubt.’ Across other texts it appears in the fixed contrast ‘great doubt, great awakening; small doubt, small awakening; no doubt, no awakening,’ in questions about ‘a person of great doubt,’ and in a biography that reports Xiuyun Wei ‘greatly doubted’ and investigated forcefully. Thus the corpus uses the phrase both as a named weight of doubt and verbally for becoming deeply doubtful; English ‘great doubt’ covers both without positing different referents.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: Great doubt is an intensified mass of inquiry cultivated until its obstruction breaks open.
